text:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: SLO alert — model-inference service p95/p99 breach detected for 'text-gen-primary' cluster. p95 = 1.82s (SLO 1.0s), p99 = 5.43s. Error budget burn high. Initial signal shows spike correlated with 'prompt_preproc' span. Paging oncall @sanjay :pager:

sanjay: I'm oncall, taking this. Confirming impact: are customers experiencing streaming stalls or full request timeouts?

alex: I'm here — noticing increased tail latency primarily for streaming sessions. Many stalls at state 'tokenize->prepare_payload'. Streaming frames stall for ~200-800ms intermittently, accumulative tail.

maria: Observed request rate normal. CPU on preproc pods jumped ~3x. Memory usage a bit up. No recent infra deploys in the last 30m.

ineesha: I can correlate with a recent change in the prompt templater PR that switched from lazy concat to full JSON validation in the preprocessor (rolled 2h ago). PR: `github.com/redwood/prompt-templates#742`.

joe: Confirming. I saw a canary deploy of `prompt-templater:v2.1.0` at ~14:22 UTC. Canary -> 20% traffic.

sanjay: OK. Hypothesis: prompt templater change increased preproc CPU and latency per request, pushing p99 up and causing streaming stalls. Plan: (1) divert traffic away from canary, (2) add short-term autoscale, (3) if needed rollback templater change.

alex: Diving into traces. Sample trace: 
```
trace_id: 0x9a3f..
spans:
  - http_request (start)
  - prompt_preproc: 740ms (JSON schema validation)
  - tokenize: 80ms
  - runtime_generate: 120ms
  - stream_flush: stalled 250ms
```
Most problematic spans show `prompt_preproc` with heavy JSON-schema validation time.

maria: Load on preproc pods (nodepool-preproc-*) shows 95th CPU 88%, 99th 98% on canary nodes. Baseline was 40-45% before.

ops-bot: Incident channel created: #incidents/1770123456 — running incident template. Severity: SLO-breach (sev-2).

sanjay: Action items: 
- @joe please rollback the canary to v2.0.4 and re-route traffic.
- @alex enable fast-path that skips schema re-validation for requests with header `X-Prevalidated: true` (we can set from proxy quickly).
- @maria increase preproc HPA min replicas by +2 for next 15m.
- @ineesha start collecting a representative set of prompt payloads for regression tests.

joe: Rolling back canary now. Command: `kubectl set image deployment/prompt-templater prompt-templater=prompt-templater:v2.0.4 -n prod`
`kubectl rollout status deployment/prompt-templater -n prod`

(joe posts rollout logs)

joe: Rollback initiated. Will update when rollout complete. :white_check_mark:

~2m later~

joe: Rollout complete. Canary removed. Starting traffic shift to stable.

alex: I patched proxy to set `X-Prevalidated: true` for streaming routes from known SDKs — enabling skip path. Pushed change to envoy and warmed routes. Patch is non-disruptive.

maria: HPA scaled additional replicas; min replicas incremented. Nodepool autoscaler also triggered +2.

alex: After rollback + proxy patch, p95 dropped to 0.98s, p99 dropped to 1.85s. Streaming stalls reduced substantially. Current error budget burn rate decaying.

nineesha: Collected 1200 prompt payloads across impacted tenants; saving to `s3://redwood-incidents/1770123456/prompts.jsonl` for postmortem and regression suite.

sanjay: Good. Next: we need a clear RCA and mitigation to prevent recurrence. Immediate mitigations worked. Long term: disable full schema validation by default in preproc; add opt-in `validate_schema=true` header; add perf tests for templater changes that include large tool schemas and `json_mode` prompts.

maria: Also suggest adding a sampling perf metric per-request that tracks preproc CPU time and whether schema validation ran. That will make regression detection earlier.

eng-runtime: Noted. We'll add an end-to-end perf test in CI that spins up a preproc instance and runs a synthetic workload with heavy tool schemas and `json_mode` templates.

sanjay: Customer impact assessment: No timeouts reported to customers, but degraded streaming UX for ~18 minutes during canary ramp. A small set of enterprise customers on streaming routes likely saw stalls (we have telemetry to identify precise tenants).

maria: I started a query to find affected tenant IDs `SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as stalls FROM telemetry.stream_frames WHERE event_time > now() - interval '1 hour' AND stall_ms > 200 GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY stalls DESC LIMIT 20;`

joe: I'll hold a rollback postmortem with the templater team. We should add a pre-deploy perf gate for templater changes.

inc-bot: Incident update logged: mitigation applied (canary rollback, proxy skip-path, autoscale). Incident severity downgraded to advisory.

alex: Follow-ups assigned: 
- Prompt-templater team: add schema-validation opt-in and perf tests (owner: @ineesha).
- Observability: alert on preproc p95 increase and add per-request preproc_time metric (owner: @maria).
- Release process: add canary traffic ramp policy + perf gate for preproc-affecting PRs (owner: @joe).

sanjay: Anything else before we close? We should run a short runbook: if p95 preproc >1.2s do: (1) divert canary, (2) set proxy header to skip validation, (3) scale preproc. I'll add to runbooks.

maria: Adding runbook notes now.

oneesha: I'll prepare regression suite and attach to PR template.

joe: I'll sync with product/security to ensure we’re OK with opt-in validation flag for sensitive customers.

inc-bot: Incident closed (incident-severity: advisory). Time to resolution ~28 minutes. Root cause: performance regression introduced by prompt-templater v2.1.0 due to always-on JSON-schema validation in preproc. Mitigations: rollback, skip-path, autoscale.

sanjay: Thanks team. I'll draft the incident postmortem and link traces/logs. Closing channel in 1h unless new signals. :thumbsup:
